Sets up the environment and acquires a database connection from the pool using the provided name, username, password, and optional parameters.
Synchronizes a cluster in distributed mode by replacing it with a new cluster, after verifying security permissions and that the database is running with an enabled distributed manager.
Returns an iterator of providers for the specified class using the Orient class loader.
Checks if the JVM heap size plus OrientDB cache size exceed physical memory and logs a warning if they do.
Creates a Vertex from a JSON object using the specified factory, mode, and property keys.
Creates an Edge from a JSON object using the given vertices, factory, mode, and property keys.
Converts an Element to a JSONObject using OGraphSONUtility, selecting property keys based on whether the element is an Edge.
Converts an Element into an ObjectNode using OGraphSONUtility, selecting property keys based on whether the element is an Edge.
Creates and runs an ETL job with the given configuration and server, validating it and tracking its execution.
Returns an ODocument containing a "jobs" field that lists the status of the current job if one exists.
Creates a map of data center names to the set of registered servers belonging to each data center.
Returns the algorithm part of a cipher transformation string (the substring before the first “/”), or null if the string contains no slash.
Creates an OSymmetricKey from a configuration by delegating to the appropriate factory method (string, file, or keystore) based on the config, or throws an exception if the config is invalid.
Reads a symmetric key from the specified file path and returns an OSymmetricKey instance, handling any I/O or parsing exceptions.
Creates an OSymmetricKey from an InputStream by reading its contents as a Base64 string and constructing a key with the specified algorithm.
Encrypts the given byte array with the specified cipher transformation and secret key, returning a JSON‑encoded string that includes the ciphertext and any initialization vector.
Writes the object's base64‑encoded key to the supplied OutputStream, checking for null, closing writers and the stream, and wrapping any errors in an OSecurityException.
Saves the secret key to a JCEKS keystore written to the provided OutputStream, using the supplied keystore password, key alias, and key password.
Sets or removes the child context, updating parent references accordingly.
Adds an object to the uniqueResult set, wrapping new ODocument instances in an ODocumentEqualityWrapper before adding.
Parses a field value string and returns either a record or a map (or an empty document/map) depending on the presence of type fields and the iNoMap flag.
Authenticates a user against a database and returns the user’s record ID, handling security and lock exceptions.
Retrieves a value from a map, optionally following a space‑delimited key path to nested maps or documents.
Returns a reused record after resetting it, or null if no reusable record is available.
Reads the current record by moving the cursor (next, previous, or staying), respecting a limit, loading it from the database, handling errors and broken IDs, and returns the record or null if none.
Returns a transactional OrientGraph, creating a new graph if no pool is available or retrieving one from the pool, then initializing it.
Returns a non‑transactional OrientGraph instance, creating it via the factory with or without a connection pool, then initializing it.
Closes any existing pool, creates a new partitioned database pool with the given max size (auto‑creating databases), applies all stored properties, and returns the factory.
Retrieves a property value by name, converting the name to lowercase using the English locale.
Stops the current transaction by committing if the conclusion is SUCCESS, otherwise rolling it back, after ensuring the database is open and the transaction is active.
Parses a statement into an OStatement AST node, building the parse tree and handling any parse or runtime exceptions.
Advances to the next token, creating a new one from the source if needed, updates internal state, and returns it.
Returns the token at the specified index, fetching new tokens from the source as needed.

Generates a ParseException by collecting all expected token indices from lookahead data, rescanning the current token, and returning the exception with the token, expected token sequences, and token images.
Retrieves an iterable of adjacent vertices in the specified direction and labels, handling single, collection, and ORidBag references lazily.
Removes the vertex from the graph, handling transaction start, index cleanup, and deletion of all connected edges.
Adds an edge with the given label to the specified vertex, unwrapping a PartitionVertex to its base vertex before delegating to the underlying addEdge implementation.
Adds an edge with the given label, incoming vertex, and class name, delegating to the full addEdge method with null outVertex and properties.
Returns the connection class name by stripping the OUT or IN prefix from the field name based on direction, or the default edge class name if no prefix applies.
Determines the edge connection class for a given direction and field name (optionally filtering by class names) and returns a pair of the direction and that class, or null if no match is found.
Reads broken record IDs from JSON, logs the count, and if link migration is enabled, removes links from imported documents for those records.
Collects and caches all public, non‑static, void methods from the application and any loaded OConsoleCommandCollection implementations, sorting them by @ConsoleCommand priority and name, into a map.
Executes a distributed task on the local node, validating the storage, running the task within a distributed scenario, logging errors, updating LSNs for replicated tasks, and handling exceptions.
Filters the given node collection to only include nodes whose status matches any of the specified statuses for the given database, then returns the count of remaining nodes.
Delegates a backup operation to the underlying implementation using the provided output stream, options, callable, listener, compression level, and buffer size.
Pauses execution for a random short delay before retrying, logging any interruption errors.
Returns the argument at the specified index from the args array, or null if the array is null or the index is out of bounds.
Counts how many of the supplied parameter names are present in the request's parameters map.
Connects to a remote server/database using the supplied credentials (optionally intercepted), sends a connect request over the network, processes the response, and returns the admin instance.
Retrieves a map of database names to configuration strings by sending a list‑databases request over the network.
Retrieves server information by sending an OServerInfoRequest and returning the parsed ODocument.
Checks whether a database exists on the remote storage by sending an existence request and returning the result.
Deletes a database by sending a drop request, forcing remote closure, and clearing thread‑local references.
Freezes the server’s remote storage of the specified type and returns the admin instance.
Sends a release database request for the specified storage type and returns the admin instance.
Retrieves the cluster configuration by sending a distributed status request, logs the response, and returns the cluster config document.
Creates an index in the database using the supplied parameters (name, type, fields, key types, collations, etc.) and returns the size of the newly created index.
Retrieves an OrientGraph, reusing an active graph if compatible, otherwise creating a new one, optionally starts a transaction, and flags whether the graph needs to be shut down.
Parses a retry count and optional wait time from the command parser, setting the retry and wait fields accordingly.
Saves a record to the database, delegating to `database.saveAll`, and on failure removes it from the local cache and rethrows or wraps the exception.
Deletes a persistent record from the database, cleaning up the local cache on failure and rethrowing or wrapping any exceptions.
Returns a Basic authentication header string with a realm based on the provided database name or a default server realm.
Authenticates a user by verifying the supplied username and password against the server’s security system and returns the username if the credentials are valid, otherwise returns null.
Checks whether a given user is authorized to execute a specified resource, returning true if the user exists, is active, and has execute permission for that resource.
Checks if the server is non‑null, attempts to shut it down, and if it’s already shutting down, pauses for 5 seconds.
Adjusts the line and column numbers of a token in the buffer to the specified new line and column values.
Writes an OBonsaiBucketPointer’s page index and page offset into storage at the given page offset.
Retrieves a bucket pointer from the given offset by reading a long and an int and constructing an OBonsaiBucketPointer.
Ends the current atomic operation, optionally rolling back, commits changes if needed, releases locks, updates counters, and returns the log sequence number.
Acquires an exclusive lock on the specified lockName for the given operation if it isn’t already locked, and records the lock in the operation.
Updates the disk cache’s maximum memory size, enforcing pinned‑page limits, and logs the change.
Attempts to bind a server socket to the first available port in the given range on the specified host, logging success or errors, and throws an exception if none succeed.
Initializes the configuration from a server config and optional parameters, then sets the socket buffer size from the configuration.
Shuts down the logger by setting a shutdown flag and invoking shutdown on the LogManager if it is a ShutdownLogManager, ignoring any class‑loading errors.
Adds a new open item to the data map, ensuring it is not already present, respecting the open‑files limit, and logs the addition.
Removes the entry for the given key, marks it retired, updates closed file count if it was open, logs the removal, and returns the removed value or null.
Acquires a closable entry for a key, ensuring it is open (or transitioning it from closed), updates its acquisition count, and logs the action.
Retrieves the value associated with the given key from the data map, returning null if the key is not present.
Clears all cached data, resets open file count, clears and zeroes read buffers and counters, empties the state buffer and LRU list, all within a lock.
Closes the entry for the given key by emptying buffers, marking the entry closed, updating the closed file count, and returns true if the key was absent or successfully closed, otherwise false.
Drains each read buffer up to its current write count, applying each entry and clearing the buffer slots.
Adds a task to the state buffer, marks the drain status as required, and attempts to drain buffers.
After reading an entry, it writes the entry into the read buffer and drains the buffers if necessary.
Writes an entry into the specified read buffer at the next available slot, updates the write counter, and returns the new counter value.
Returns the smallest power of two greater than or equal to the given value, capped at 2^30.

Handles a live query push request by activating the database, processing error or event data, invoking listener callbacks for create, update, delete events, and handling end of stream, then restoring the previous database context.
Converts the value for a given key from the underlying map into the corresponding enum constant and stores it in the current map if it isn’t already present.
Converts all entries in the underlying map to enum constants of enumClass (using numeric indices or string names) and marks the conversion as complete.
Retrieves the binary serializer for the specified type from the serializer map.
Initializes the shutdown queue by registering handlers for workers, OrientDB instances, pending threads, profiler, and call listeners.
Retrieves an engine by name in a thread‑safe manner using a read lock.
Toggles database profiling on or off, returning performance statistics or an error if profiling was not started.
Toggles storage profiling on or off, starting or stopping performance statistics collection and returning the result or collected statistics.
Creates a new ReadersEntry with a fresh state, registers it in the readers state list, clears the state array reference, and returns the entry.

Authenticates a user from a token by validating the token, retrieving the user (or username) from the database, ensuring the account is active, and returning the user or throwing an exception if any check fails.
Creates database metadata for users and roles, ensuring identity, role, and user classes exist, and creates default admin role and user if missing, then returns the admin user.
Attempts to acquire a read lock within a timeout, handling reentrancy, waiting on a locked node, and returning true on success or false if the timeout expires.
Returns the adjacent vertex in the specified direction (OUT or IN) from the current graph, throwing an exception for unsupported directions.
Overrides getId to return a temporary ID composed of vOut and vIn identities when rawElement is null, otherwise sets the current graph in thread local and returns the superclass ID.
Sets a property on the element, first ensuring the current graph is set in thread local, converting a lightweight edge to a document if necessary, then delegating to the superclass implementation.
Removes a property from a non‑lightweight edge, returning the removed value, or null if the element is lightweight.
Clears the entire tree by resetting the root bucket, deleting all sub‑trees, and performing the operation atomically with exclusive locking.
Deletes the file by recycling its subtrees within an atomic operation, acquiring an exclusive lock and rolling back if an exception occurs.
Finalizes a batch import by launching parallel jobs, waiting for all to finish, and then cleaning up database resources and re‑enabling WAL.
Adds a vertex to the graph, updating the last vertex ID and initializing its outgoing edge list if it does not already exist.
Parses a strategy keyword, sets the traversal strategy on the current traverse object, and returns true if successful, otherwise returns false or throws an exception for an invalid strategy.
Extracts the start offset and length of each element in an embedded collection from a byte buffer, returning a list of RecordInfo objects.
Executes an insert or index update command: it creates new documents or updates an index with supplied records, saves them, and returns the created or updated items.
Determines whether a given field value is a valid OIdentifiable link that is either empty, non‑persistent, or has no connected record, returning true in those cases.
Casts the given record to ORecordAbstract, fills it with the provided RID, version, buffer, and dirty flag, and returns the updated record.
Sets the version of the given record to the specified integer.
Returns the record type byte of an ORecord, retrieving it directly if the record is an ORecordAbstract or via its underlying record otherwise.
Initializes or reopens a distributed database instance, retrying up to 100 times and shutting down the manager if the database cannot be opened.
Logs an exception’s stack trace at the specified level and returns the trace as a string.
Returns null for the given index query.
Converts an ORID link into its actual record, replacing the link in the map with the record while updating tracking and ignoring missing records.
Registers an OServerCommand instance into rest, wildcard, or exact command maps based on its names and configures it.
Creates an OServerUserConfiguration from a user document when it contains username and resources, using the provided password or an empty string if none.
Analyzes a filter condition to generate and return a list of index search results sorted by descending field count.
Creates an index search result for a field condition, handling inversion and operator conversion, or returns null if the condition cannot be indexed.
Attaches an object by traversing its class hierarchy, updating each non‑transient, non‑id, non‑version field via `setValue`, and skipping proxy classes and the `ODocument` base class.
Retrieves the OClass from the database schema by the stored className, returning null if className is null or throwing an exception if the class cannot be found.
Returns the next sequence value, synchronizing locally and updating cache if not distributed, or sending a distributed sequence action otherwise.
Truncates all records of the class by clearing its clusters, resetting its indexes, and rebuilding inherited indexes, after performing security checks.
Adds a base class to the current class, ensuring no recursion, updating the subclass list and polymorphic cluster IDs, and returns the current class.
Merges the polymorphic cluster IDs from a base class into this class, ensuring uniqueness, adding each to indexes, and updating the internal cluster ID array.
Serializes a linked record reference into a string buffer, handling ORID, String, or OIdentifiable inputs, validating the link, and optionally returning the record ID.
Releases a pointer by removing it from tracking if enabled, then either deallocates it if the pool is full or returns it to the pool for reuse.
Checks for unreleased direct memory pointers in the mapping and asserts that none are found.
Deallocates all pointers in the pointersPool and pointerMapping, clears both collections, and resets the pool size counter to zero.
Converts four consecutive bytes from a byte array starting at a given offset into a single big‑endian 32‑bit integer.

Handles opening a database by verifying it’s related to the local server, checking offline status, retrieving its configuration, restoring the thread‑local database context, and throwing an offline node exception on Hazelcast errors.
Installs clusters for a given class in a distributed database, registering the database and creating the necessary clusters across available nodes, returning true if successful.
Logs the current distributed server status if it has changed since the last dump.
Finds the index of the first element in the array that is equal to the given Comparable object, or returns -1 if not found.
Returns the index of the specified integer in the array, or -1 if it is not present.
Collects and returns the set of cluster names involved in the parsed target, filtering by user access and handling sub‑queries, single records, target classes, target clusters, and target indexes.
Handles a query result record by applying skip logic, adding it to the result set, and determining whether to continue searching.
Returns a temporary RID counter, delegating to a parent query if present, otherwise increments and returns a local serial counter.
Reports a tip to the profiler and stores it in a context list of tips.
Parses the keyword “fetchplan”, extracts the following fetch‑plan expression from the query text, assigns it to the request, and returns true if the keyword was found.
Checks if the input string equals the 'NOCACHE' keyword, sets the noCache flag if so, and returns whether it matched.
Attempts to optimize sorting by retrieving an index cursor for the given schema class, fetching values if available, and returning whether the optimization succeeded.
Returns a status document containing the current configuration, status, and log, and notifies listeners when the status is finished.
Executes a database command with the supplied arguments, sets async replication callbacks, and returns the command’s result.
Logs a JVM error if it hasn't been logged before.
Validates and inserts a key-value pair into an index, handling transaction context, locking, disk space and read‑only checks, and logging/rethrowing any exceptions.
Rolls back the active micro‑transaction if it matches the given one, marks the storage dirty, rolls back storage changes, updates caches, clears the transaction state, and handles any errors.

Executes a text command by obtaining an executor, setting its context and progress listener, parsing the command, and running it, retrying on ORetryQueryException and rethrowing any runtime, error, or throwable after logging.
Registers a cluster, ensuring no duplicate name, adding it to the cluster map, and returns its ID.
Sets or removes a property in the map using a lowercased key and returns the previous value.
Creates a class in the database schema if it doesn’t already exist (or if the ifNotExists flag is false) and returns the total number of classes in the schema.
Executes a sync database command by verifying distributed mode and security, then installs the database with optional force and full‑sync options.
Deletes a record by its ID and version, then returns the database instance.
Executes the appropriate record hooks for a given record and type, respecting distributed execution modes, and returns the resulting hook outcome (changed, skipped, replaced, or unchanged).
Deletes the record identified by the given ORID from the database (if it exists) and returns the database instance.
Counts the number of records in the specified view by retrieving the view metadata and delegating to countClass.
Counts the number of records for a given class name, optionally including subclasses, throwing an exception if the class is not found.
Sets this database instance as the current thread’s database and returns the instance.
Registers an encryption algorithm, ensuring no duplicate names in the registry, and logs an error if registration fails.
Finds the index of the byte just before the given absolute position within the binary chunk that contains that position.
Parses an optional word, updates parser positions, and returns the word string or null if no word is found.
Parses the next word (using optional separators), throws a syntax error with a custom message if none is found, and returns the word trimmed of leading/trailing spaces if present.

Parses the next characters from the input, matching them against a list of candidate words and returning the index of the matched word (or -1 if none), throwing a syntax error if a match is mandatory.
Parses an optional keyword from the input, returning true if a specified keyword is found (or throwing a syntax error if an unexpected keyword appears), and returns false if no keyword is present.
Checks if a given character is among the specified separator characters, updates parserLastSeparator if it matches, and returns true if found or false otherwise.

Drops a database class, optionally checking for existence, preventing deletion of non‑empty vertex or edge classes unless the UNSAFE flag is set, and logs warnings when dropping such classes in unsafe mode.
Deletes the configuration file and its backup from storage if they exist.
Returns the offset of the next byte array in the buffer and advances the read position past its header and data, or -1 if the end of the buffer is reached.
Returns a formatted string combining the given token type and the OAuth2 access token value.
Acquires an OAuth2 access token for a resource, managing context state and existing tokens, and throws exceptions if the token cannot be obtained.
Copies the OAuth2 access token from the current security context into the context if none exists, returning true on success.
Checks if the input stream has no more characters to read, returning true when the stream is exhausted.
Reads a line into the provided byte array using the given line terminators.
Reads up to len bytes into the array, stopping at LF, CR, or CRLF terminators, and returns the number of bytes read (or –1 if end of stream).
Skips the specified number of bytes by reading them into a buffer and returns the number of bytes actually skipped.
Skips up to n bytes, first consuming any buffered data, then using the underlying stream (or reading if skip fails) while updating position, available bytes, and read byte count.
Validates that a given offset and length are within the bounds of an array, throwing exceptions for negative values or out-of-range indices.
In-place merge sort on a subarray using a comparator and swapper, with insertion sort for small ranges and early exit if halves are already sorted.
Swaps two contiguous blocks of length n by repeatedly calling the provided Swapper on corresponding positions.
Sorts a subarray in parallel using a ForkJoinPool and a generic quicksort task.
Computes a 32‑bit MurmurHash3 hash of the input integer.
Computes a 64‑bit MurmurHash3 hash of the input long value.
Writes data from a ByteBuffer into an internal buffer and, if needed, to a file channel, updating write positions and returning the number of bytes read.
Truncates the file to the larger of the specified size or the current write position.
Sets the stream’s position to the specified value, flushing first and using a repositionable stream or file channel if available, otherwise throwing an exception.
Attempts to report consumer refresh metrics, logging any exceptions without interrupting the refresh process.
Waits for all current tasks to finish successfully and clears the task list.
Finds matching records for a query and returns a stream of selected fields.
Collects and returns the set of schema names that are compaction candidates and have no dependencies on any other targeted schemas.
Deletes snapshot files older than the configured number to keep, logging any failures.
Computes the hash code of a specified field in a Hollow object by reading the field value according to its type and applying the appropriate hash function.
Compares two fields from possibly different objects for equality, handling primitive, byte array, string, and reference types.
Removes references to matched schemas that lie outside the closure by iterating schemas in reverse dependency order and invoking traverseReferencesOutsideClosure for each such reference.
Collects and reports metrics for a completed announcement, recording success status, data size, duration, and the timestamp of the last successful announcement.
Updates cycle success/failure counters, records timing, and reports cycle metrics.
Reads a count of UTF key/value pairs from a DataInputStream and returns them as a Map<String,String>.
Extracts a RecordPrimaryKey from an object by mapping its type and primary key.
Clears all bits in the bit set by setting every long in each segment to zero.
Reads a sequence of longs from a DataInputStream, treating each as a 64‑bit bitmap of populated ordinals, and notifies listeners for each block of 64 ordinals.
Returns the current size of the sparse bit set, retrying until a consistent snapshot is obtained.

Returns a string representation of a field’s value from a diff view row, handling leaf nodes (replacing ‘|’ with a special character and showing “null” for null values) and non‑leaf nodes (showing the type name and a “ [null]” suffix if the value is null).
Copies a specified number of bytes from a source ByteData at a given source position to a destination position.
Copies a specified number of bytes from a segmented source buffer starting at a given position into a destination byte array, returning the number of bytes copied.
Returns true if the specified range of bytes in this array matches the specified range in another SegmentedByteArray, otherwise false.
Copies a specified range of bytes from a source segmented byte array into this array, handling segment boundaries and ensuring capacity.
Copies a specified number of bytes from a segmented source starting at srcPos into a destination byte array at destPos, handling segment boundaries, and returns the number of bytes copied.
Reads a specified number of bytes from an InputStream into internal segments, ensuring capacity and copying data in segment-sized chunks.
Writes a specified range of bytes from a segmented data structure to an OutputStream.
Ensures the segments array can hold the given index, expanding it if necessary, and initializes the segment at that index with a new byte array if it is null.
Returns the index of the specified field name from a lookup map, or -1 if the field name is not present.

Deduplicates ordinals per list, updates matchIndexHashAndSizeArray with unique counts, sums hash table sizes, tracks the maximum unique count, and returns the total bucket count combined with the bit width needed to represent that maximum.
Checks whether the given dataset contains any list, set, or map schemas.
Generates Java source files for a Hollow API—including the API class, factory, hash index, and schema files—placing them in the specified directory.
Generates source files for each dataset schema, creating API, object, factory, delegate, accessor, and primary‑key index classes as dictated by the schema type and configuration.
Checks if the supplied keys match the expected field path indexes for the given ordinal.
Returns an array of key field values for the record at the specified ordinal.
Creates a FieldPath of ObjectFieldSegment for a primary key, stripping a trailing “!” if present, auto‑expanding as needed, and asserting all segments are ObjectFieldSegment.
Creates a FieldPath for a hash index using the given dataset, type, and path.
Creates a FieldPath for a prefix index, optionally auto‑expanding segments and requiring a full path when autoExpand is false.
Stores an object with its ordinal in the appropriate segment based on its identity hash code.
Initializes internal state by computing total words, average word length, and max ordinal for the last reference type, then builds a prefix index.
Checks if the given key is present by delegating to the current prefix index, retrying until the prefix index reference stabilizes.
Calculates the absolute percentage change between two cardinality values.
Adds a field to the configuration for a given type, creating a new config if one does not already exist.
Returns a list of schemas sorted in dependency order based on their inter-schema dependencies.

Initializes default configuration flags for the next major version, enabling package grouping, boolean ergonomics, primary‑key index reservation, hollow primitive types, API restriction to field types, and verbose toString.
Retrieves a long value from a segmented array by index, returning 0 if the segment is missing or the index is out of bounds.
Finds matching records across all type states for a given field name and value, aggregating results into a map of type names to BitSets.
Finds records of the specified type whose given field matches the provided value, returning a map of matching record IDs to BitSets.
Resets results, assigns the provided paths to elementPaths, and clears elementKeyPaths and elementNonKeyPaths.
Sets the element key paths, validating each against known element paths and updating the key and non‑key BitSet masks accordingly.
Calculates matches between two data sets in parallel by traversing matched and unmatched elements, populating hash tables, and counting matches.
Restores the data model to the most recent announced version if one is available.
Runs a data synchronization cycle by applying mutations, updating the version, notifying listeners of success or failure, and cleaning up state.
Marks the ordinal that matches the given key in the specified primary key index as excluded by setting its bit in the corresponding BitSet.

Collects all state engines from the excluded ordinals, then for each engine expands the excluded set to include all transitive references by adding transitive matches and updates the excludedOrdinals map accordingly.
Writes a HollowBlobHeader to a DataOutputStream, including the version header, random tags, schemas, a backward‑compatibility envelope, and header tags.
Calculates and aggregates heap footprint and populated ordinal counts for each type in the given HollowReadStateEngine, storing totals and per‑type metrics.
Writes all field data to the given ByteDataBuffer by iterating over fieldData and calling writeField for each element.
Writes a 32‑bit integer to a ByteDataBuffer in big‑endian byte order.
Writes a long value to a ByteDataBuffer in big‑endian byte order.
Adds an ordinal to the free pool, expanding the array if it is full.
Sorts the freeOrdinals array from index 0 to size and then reverses it to produce a descending order.
Computes a combined hash code for an array of objects and their corresponding field types by iteratively multiplying the current hash by 31 and XOR‑ing it with the hash of each element.
Computes a hash code for a key based on its FieldType, handling ints, longs, references, bytes, strings, booleans, doubles, and floats.
Resizes the internal storage array to a larger capacity by allocating a new array, copying existing elements, and replacing the old storage.
Returns a free ordinal, preferring the specified one if it is unused, otherwise obtaining a new free ordinal.
Builds an array mapping each ordinal to its pointer value from the pointersAndOrdinals array, preparing the data for writing.
Compares a serialized representation against the bytes stored at a key‑derived position in the buffer, returning true only if the lengths and all bytes match.
Doubles the key array size, checks for overflow, and delegates to the overloaded growKeyArray method.
Recomputes the hash code for data previously added at the given key by locating its position, reading its size, and hashing the corresponding bytes.
Creates an AtomicLongArray of the given size, initializing all elements to EMPTY_BUCKET_VALUE, and returns it.
Checks whether the match at matchIdx in this traverser is equal to the match at otherMatchIdx in another traverser across all field paths.
Finds a matching record for the given key by extracting key fields, looking up an ordinal, and returning the corresponding type or null if no match is found.
Creates a ReadStateHelper with the current and pending state engines swapped.

Computes the size of a hash table as the next power of two that can hold the given number of elements (using a 0.7 load factor), validating that the element count is non‑negative and within the maximum allowed size.
Runs a compaction cycle with the given config if compaction is needed, otherwise returns NO_ANNOUNCEMENT_AVAILABLE.
Writes a snapshot of the current state engine to the given OutputStream, including headers, schemas, and type snapshots, by concurrently calculating snapshots and serializing them.
Writes a delta of changed data types to an output stream by preparing the state engine, calculating deltas concurrently, and serializing the updated schemas and their deltas.
Adds non‑primitive, non‑collection schema names to the provided set.
Converts a dotted field path into a camelCase parameter name by lowercasing the first segment, capitalizing subsequent segments, and removing a trailing exclamation mark.
Rebuilds the hash index by creating a new builder, building the index, and updating the volatile hash state.
Finds a matching entry in a concurrent hash index for the given query objects, returning a result or null if none is found.
Triggers an asynchronous refresh after a random delay up to the specified maximum.
Schedules an asynchronous refresh of the HollowClient after a specified delay, sleeping until the target time before invoking triggerRefresh, and logs any failures.
Creates a HollowTypeDiff for the given type and primary key paths, stores it in the map if it contains data, and returns the diff.
Prepares for diff calculation, logs the preparation time, and then calculates diffs for each typeDiff.
Writes a long value to an OutputStream using a variable‑length encoding with continuation bits.
Writes an integer to an OutputStream using a 5‑byte variable‑length encoding, setting the high bit on all but the last byte.
Encodes an integer into a variable‑length byte sequence (up to five bytes with continuation bits) and returns the updated write position.
Reads a variable‑length integer from an InputStream, throwing an exception if a null marker (0x80) is encountered.
Reads a variable‑length encoded long from an InputStream, throwing an exception if a null marker (0x80) is encountered.
Adds a child view at a specified index with given layout parameters by delegating to the superclass implementation.
Adjusts header and footer loading view dimensions and view padding according to the pull‑to‑refresh scroll direction and whether the loading layouts are shown.
